verdict.rationale: Composio's docs show concrete mechanisms for scoping agent credentials: sessions can be restricted to specific `toolkits` (composio-docs-3), MCP servers can be created with `allowed_tools` lists per toolkit and `auth_config` (composio-docs-23, composio-docs-5), and by default a session has broad access but this can be explicitly restricted (composio-docs-35). This directly matches issuing least-privilege credentials for an agent's runtime. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on verification that scoping is enforced correctly in production, and the community report of a leaked Composio key yielding live Gmail/GitHub/CircleCI tokens (composio-comm-2) raises some doubt about how tightly scoped real-world keys end up being, reducing confidence.
